description: The canonical errors of the SDKs (sdks/SPEC.md §2). Each SDK embeds a copy of this file; a test proves the copy equals it. `retryable` is the default for an error the server did not classify itself.

errors.remediation: The request is malformed: check the fields and their types against the API reference.
The token was refused: check its issuer, audience, tenant claim and expiry, and that the token provider returns a fresh one.
The identity may not do this: ask an administrator for the role or permission the call needs.
The resource does not exist in this tenant and namespace: check the id and the namespace.
The request conflicts with the current state: read the resource again and decide; do not repeat it unchanged.
A field is invalid: the reason names it. Fix the input; repeating it fails the same way.
Too many requests: wait for Retry-After and slow down.
A quota of the tenant or namespace is exhausted: free capacity or ask an administrator to raise it.
The service could not serve the request now: retry with the same idempotency key after a short wait.
An unexpected error on the server: retry once, and if it persists report the trace id to the operator.

The platform operator has not recorded the instance registry requirement this needs (code-workflows-v1 for a code version, signal-inbox-v1 for one that declares signals): ask the operator to record it once every instance reports the capability.
The run's code version does not declare this signal: send a declared signal name, or publish and move to a version that declares it.
The run holds as many pending signals of this name as its version allows: retry after the workflow has consumed some.
The run is near its history limit and takes no more signals or updates: send them to the run's successor after it continues as new.
The run is about to end and is not taking new signals or updates: retry later, or send them to the run that follows it.
The update was admitted but has not completed within the wait: read its receipt later, or send it again with acceptPending.
The run, or this caller's share of it, has as many open updates as it may hold: retry after some complete, honouring retry-after-ms.
The run is stopping or has ended and cannot take this request: check the run's status.
No worker answered the query within its timeout: check that a worker serves the run's code digest, or use a declared query, which needs no worker.
The query handler tried to change the workflow: a worker query must only read the workflow's state.
The run cannot answer a worker query now (its namespace's workflow tasks are paused, it is under review, or it has ended): use a declared query, or retry once it runs again.
The target is not a published code version of the run's own workflow: check the version number.
The update handler returned a result outside the update's declared resultSchema: fix the handler; the update failed and the run went on.
The run ended before the update completed: the update was finished by the platform; send it to another run if it still applies.
The run continued as new before the update completed: send the update again to the chain, which addresses the run that follows.
The run kept working while its move was being checked: pause the namespace's workflow tasks and request the move again.
No worker of the target code digest took the replay check within an hour: start a worker of the target version and request the move again.
The run's history does not replay to the same commands on the target code: the run stays on its version; see the first difference and guard the change with patched.
Work the run still has open does not fit the target version's envelope or declarations: the run stays on its version; publish a target that keeps them.
The run's history replays to the same commands on the target code: a move of this run would apply.
The replay check of this run was abandoned by its workers three times: check the target version's workers and request the move again.
The workflow failed itself with a code outside the allowed pattern: use a code matching ^[A-Z][A-Z0-9_]{0,63}$ in the workflow failure.
The lease is no longer current (it expired, was reclaimed or the run ended): stop working on this task and do not report it.
This idempotency key was used for a different request: use a new key for a new request.
The worker identity is not bound to this namespace and activity: ask an administrator to bind it with a worker binding.
A secret the step declares does not exist or its publisher may no longer use it: check the secret and its access list.
The server does not speak this major version of the worker protocol: upgrade or downgrade the SDK.
The table or the target ref does not exist: create it in the catalog first; the platform never creates tables.
The step cannot write this table (format version, file format, partition transform or key): see the reason and use a table the step supports.
A table, data or metadata location is outside the connection's warehouse locations: fix the table location or add the prefix to the connection.
A record does not map losslessly to the table schema: check the mapping, the column types and the required columns named in the failure.
The batch holds the same key twice: remove the duplicates before the write.
A row is outside the overwrite filter, or the batch is empty without allowEmpty: check the filter and the records.
Concurrent commits kept the write from landing: it is retried; reduce the writers to the table if it persists.
A later commit changed what this step wrote, so it cannot be reverted automatically: review the table and resolve the step by hand.
The write is over a records, bytes, files or columns limit: split the batch or raise the limit within the platform ceiling.
The catalog could not be reached: check its address, credentials and availability; the step is retried.
The object storage could not be reached or is throttling: check it; the step is retried.
The destination key has no primary key or unique constraint: add the constraint or choose a key it covers.
A destination column is missing or cannot hold a value: check the mapping and the column types.
The retry is outside the destination's deduplication window, so a duplicate cannot be ruled out: resolve the step by hand.
An object with this name and different content already exists: check the destination prefix; the platform never overwrites it.
The delivery is over a message size, count or bytes limit: send fewer or smaller records.
The subscription also carries run events: use a subscription whose purpose is STEP_OUTPUT.
The destination refused the credentials: check the secret the connection names and the access it grants.
The destination could not be reached or is overloaded: check it; the step is retried.
The subscription is disabled, deleted or below a field's classification level: fix the subscription and retry the step.
A destination whose policy is fail did not complete: see the destination's own code in the failure detail.
The sandboxed lake host broke its protocol: the step is retried; report the trace id if it persists.
The sandbox for the attempt could not be started: check the sandbox runner and its capacity; the step is retried.
A field is above the connection's classification ceiling, or is a secret: lower the field's level or raise the ceiling with the reveal grant.
Whether the write happened is unknown: do not repeat it blindly; check the destination and resolve the step.
The workflow code made other commands on replay than the run recorded: the run is under review; move it to fixed code, reset it or cancel it.
The commands of the completion do not reproduce the run's command chain: the run is under review; retry it on another worker, move it, reset it or cancel it.
The workflow left the deterministic runtime or answered before its window: the run is under review; retry, move, reset or cancel it.
A command is outside the code version's envelope: the run is under review; publish a version whose envelope covers it and move the run.
A command is malformed or not allowed in the run's state: the run is under review; fix the code and move the run, reset it or cancel it.
An update validator issued a command: validators must only read; the run is under review; fix the code and move the run.
The workflow code threw an exception that is not a workflow failure: it is retried with a backoff, and after five failures in a row the run goes under review.
The workflow code did not yield within the activation deadline: look for a busy loop or blocking call; it counts as a workflow task failure.
No completion arrived within the workflow task timeout: it is retried with a backoff and counts as a workflow task failure.
A value held for a deferred command was released before it was used: the workflow task is retried and uploads the value again.
The workflow task uploaded more than 16 command values: pass fewer large values per activation; it counts as a workflow task failure.
The run has 2,048 steps that can still act: wait for some to finish, or move a large fan-out to a graph child.
The terminal command waits for open work of the run to settle; nothing to do, it is applied when it settles.
The terminal command waits until the workflow has seen the events that arrived meanwhile; nothing to do.
Only commands that wind the run down are allowed after its history limit: the run is under review; move it to code that ends or continues it, or cancel it.
The run's history reached its limit: retry the review to open the closing window, in which the workflow should continue as new or end.
The run would retain more than 4 MiB: keep large values in blobs or continue as new; the run is under review, or the update failed.
The tenant's content quota refused the values of the completion: free stored content or raise the quota; it counts as a workflow task failure.
The value is withheld because its carrier classifies a field secret, or because the export never carries a blob: a secret field is never revealed; read a blob through the activity that owns it.
No answer from the server: check the URL, the network and the TLS settings; the call is retried when it is safe.
The call was cancelled by the caller.
The server's answer did not match the contract: update the SDK, and report the trace id if it persists.
The payload is over the limit (256 KiB inline): send a smaller output.
One activation made more than 256 commands or 48 KiB of command metadata: catch it, or move the fan-out to a graph child.
The values of one activation do not fit its message: pass smaller values, fewer gated inputs, or continue as new with a smaller state.
The replayer reached a value withheld from the export: the replay is neither a match nor a mismatch from that command on; export with the reveal rights.
